Selection quality tests a predeclared distinguishing observable; question coverage is coverage of these tasks only.
Definition repeatability recompiles identical designs; it does not measure simulator replay or experimental reproducibility.
No experiments run in this procedural benchmark. Token counts remain unknown when the participant does not report them.
Wilson intervals and the paired p-value use binomial and exchangeability assumptions. Deterministic related fixtures do not establish those assumptions or justify population inference.
Activation requires a two-sided paired p <= 0.05 improvement without aggregate metric regression, plus operator review; this is a procedural gate, not proof of external scientific validity.

design.competing_hypothesis: Periodic driving does not increase RMS displacement over this window.
design.question: Does periodic driving increase displacement against an otherwise matched free oscillator?

controls: matched mass, damping, stiffness, clock and initial conditions
ir.hypothesis: Driving will increase RMS displacement by at least 0.01 m relative to a matched zero-force control.
limitations: Simulation of m x'' + b x' + k x = F cos(omega t), not physical measurements.
Linear underdamped dynamics only; no nonlinearities, thermal noise or physical equipment.
RMS compares the complete preregistered sampled window including transients.
Reference accuracy establishes numerical agreement, not empirical validity of the model.
Same-runtime replay is byte-deterministic; cross-engine floating point identity is not promised.

observables.description: Treatment RMS displacement minus matched control RMS

parameter_constraints: sample interval resolves fastest period at >= 8 samples per period
ir.question: How does cosine driving change RMS displacement against a matched zero-force oscillator?

statistical_analysis.method: Difference of sampled trajectory RMS; analytic reference verifies every integration step
statistical_analysis.uncertainty: Deterministic simulation, one matched initial condition; temporal samples are correlated. Maximum analytic error is reported; no population inference or p-value.
